1 1/4 cups water, room temperature
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
about 1 tsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

1. Dissolve the yeast in about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons water.

2. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

3. Add the yeast water.

4. Knead for 3–4 minutes.

5. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

6. Gradually add the salted water.

7. Add the olive oil.

8. Knead for about 10 minutes by hand or 8 minutes in a mixer, until smooth.

9. Shape into a ball.

10. Cover.

11. Rest for 1 hour.

12. Divide into 8 equal pieces.

13. Roll into ropes about 8–9 inches long.

14. Join each rope into a ring.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Cover.

17. Proof for 1–1 1/2 hours, until nearly doubled.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Bake for 20–25 minutes.

20. Remove from the oven.

21. Wait 5 minutes.

22. Cut each ring horizontally in half with a serrated knife or strong thread.

23. Arrange the 16 halves cut-side up.

24. Reduce a convection oven to 300°F.

25. Bake for another 35–45 minutes, until completely dry.

26. Cool on a rack.

Service

The second bake should remove nearly all moisture, which is what gives friselle their long shelf life.

Calabrian red-wine and citrus yeast pastries, fried and coated in cinnamon sugar.

1/2 cup warm whole milk

1 tsp fine salt

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with 1 teaspoon of the sugar.

5. Add the eggs.

15. Cover.

16. Proof for another 2 hours.

17. Mix the finishing sugar with the cinnamon.

18. Heat the oil to 340°F.

19. Fry only a few pastries at a time for about 5–6 minutes total, turning several times.

20. Drain on paper towels.

21. Coat in cinnamon sugar while still hot.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Moderate frying heat lets the thick egg-rich dough cook through before the exterior becomes too dark.

1 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Knead until the dough begins to become smooth.

5. Add the salt.

6. Add the olive oil.

7. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until uniform and elastic.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise until doubled, about 1 1/2–2 hours.

10. Dust a baking sheet with the flour.

11. Turn the dough onto the work surface.

12. Shape into a ball.

13. Make a hole in the center.

14. Gently widen into a broad flattened ring.

15. Transfer to the baking sheet.

16. Cover.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and deeply golden.

20. Cool slightly on a rack.

23. Continue baking for 50–60 minutes, until the crust is thick and crisp.

24. Cool completely on a rack.

Ingredients

3 cups bread flour or all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cups cold water
1/4 tsp active dry yeast
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Put the flour, yeast, and salt in a stand-mixer bowl.

2. Mix briefly with the paddle.

3. Slowly add the cold water.

4. Mix into a very soft sticky dough.

5. Alternatively, stir vigorously with a wooden spoon.

6. Cover the bowl well.

7. Ferment in a warm place overnight, about 10–12 hours.

8. Lightly flour the work surface.

9. Turn out the dough gently.

10. Without kneading, fold the edges toward the center and shape into a ball.

11. Flour a clean kitchen towel generously.

12. Put the loaf on the towel.

13. Cover.

14. Proof for 1–2 hours.

15. About 30 minutes before the proof ends, put a covered cast-iron pot in the oven.

16. Preheat the oven and pot to 450°F.

17. Carefully remove the hot pot.

18. Gently invert the dough into the pot.

19. Cover immediately.

20. Bake for 30 minutes.

21. Remove the lid.

22. Continue baking for 15–20 minutes, until deeply golden.

23. Turn the loaf onto a rack.

24. Cool completely before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The overnight fermentation with very little yeast develops flavor without requiring intensive kneading.
